en: The highest recorded temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley, almost twice the average temperature in Manila.
It takes natural processes about 500 years to form one inch of topsoil, roughly the thickness of three stacked smartphones.
A single cubic meter of granite weighs about 2,700 kilograms, making it roughly three times heavier than the same volume of liquid water.
A large cumulonimbus thundercloud can weigh over 500,000 kilograms, which is approximately equal to the combined weight of 100 adult African elephants.
You could fit about 1.3 million Earths inside the Sun, which has a massive diameter of 1.39 million kilometers.
Proxima Centauri is the closest star to our solar system, located 4.24 light-years away, equaling roughly 40 trillion kilometers.
The Moon's diameter is 3,474 kilometers, making it one-quarter the size of Earth and roughly the width of Australia.
The 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption ejected 10 cubic kilometers of material, cooling the global average temperature by 0.5 degrees Celsius.
Typhoon Haiyan produced sustained winds of 280 kilometers per hour, nearly three times the maximum speed limit on a Philippine expressway.
Antarctica holds about 90 percent of Earth's ice, containing more fresh water than all the world's lakes and rivers combined.
Quartz makes up about 12 percent of Earth's continental crust by volume, meaning roughly one-eighth of the crust is this mineral.
The Moon moves away from Earth at 3.8 centimeters per year, which is about the same speed human fingernails grow.
